rev_growth.label: Revenue growth YoY
rev_growth.why: Demand strength this quarter vs. a year ago.

rev_accel.label: Revenue acceleration
rev_accel.why: Change in YoY growth vs. last quarter — semis stocks tend to turn when growth inflects.

gm_change.label: Gross-margin change YoY
gm_change.why: Rising margins = pricing power / better utilization (cycle upswing).

inv_days_change.label: Inventory-days change YoY
inv_days_change.why: Falling days of inventory = channel is lean; a rising pile is the classic downturn warning.

op_margin_change.label: Operating-margin change YoY
op_margin_change.why: Operating leverage: in an upswing, fixed costs get spread over more sales and margins jump.

fcf_margin.label: FCF margin (TTM)
fcf_margin.why: Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) per dollar of sales — real cash, not accounting profit.

rd_intensity.label: R&D intensity (TTM)
rd_intensity.why: R&D spend / sales. Informational only (weight 0) — shown in the report card so you can see if it predicts anything before trusting it.

capex_intensity.label: Capex intensity (TTM)
capex_intensity.why: Capex / sales. Informational only (weight 0). Heavy capex late in a cycle often precedes oversupply.

sales_yield.label: Sales yield (TTM sales / mkt cap)
sales_yield.why: Inverse of price-to-sales: how much revenue you buy per dollar. Higher = cheaper. Split-safe (uses SEC share counts in split-adjusted units).

momentum.label: Price momentum (6-1 mo)
momentum.why: 6-month return skipping the latest month; trend persistence.

low_vol.label: Volatility (6 mo)
low_vol.why: Annualized daily volatility; lower is preferred as a mild tie-breaker.

oos.summary: 2 of 9 scored stats held up after 2020. Flipped: Price momentum (6-1 mo). Pointing the wrong way in both periods (consider weight 0): Volatility (6 mo). Combined score: held up. Strategy beat SPY by 39.1%/yr out of sample.

start_luck.read: Starting on a different date moves CAGR between 34% and 46% (12 starts). The 43.7% headline sits mid-pack, so it isn't a lucky start.

decay.read: The edge keeps building after 3 months (peaks at 12 months, +13.7%): holding longer might work as well with less trading.

streak_edge.read: Stocks still picked from the previous quarter beat the average stock by +5.6% a quarter (140 picks); newly picked ones by +0.8% (150 picks). Over 55 quarters the stayers came out ahead (t 2.5): a streak looks like it means something.

bands.read: For a 5-day, 90% net, the best single method was "Recent-weighted" (held 89% of the time). The plain bell curve held 91%. The weighted blend held 91% and the equal average 90%.

backtest.label: backtest
backtest.explain: Over 59 quarters the strategy beat SPY by +7.1% per quarter on average (t = 3.8). If there were no real edge, luck alone would produce a result this good less than 1 time in 100. A 90% range for the yearly edge is +18% to +52%.  Caution: this is a backtest of a model designed knowing the past, so it overstates the evidence. The live paper portfolio is the real test.

dsr.explain: We tried 22 versions of the strategy. Even with zero skill, the best of 22 would show a Sharpe of about 0.11 by luck, so the baseline's 1.20 gets haircut to 1.09. After adjusting for that, the chance its true Sharpe is above zero is over 99%. Caveat: this only counts the variants in the robustness table, not the earlier choices of which stats to use, so the true haircut is bigger.

backtest.label: backtest
backtest.read: Beat SPY in 86% of 1-year windows; worst stretch Apr 2024–Apr 2025 at −45% vs SPY. Expect at least one year like that. Information ratio 1.05 (above 0.5 is good for a stock picker).

drawdowns.read: The worst drop (−53%, 2024-06 to 2025-04) took 15 months to get back to the old high; SOXX fell 41% in the same stretch and took 14 months. It spent 31% of all days more than 10% below its previous high.

outcomes.read: Replaying the backtest's 59 quarters in random 1-year blocks, $1,000 became $2,870 to $16,263 after 5 years in 8 of 10 replays (middle: $6,332). After 1 year it was below $1,000 in 9% of replays, and it beat SPY over 5 years in 98%. The worst 1 in 20 replays fell 31% or more at some point. This replays the past; it is not a forecast.
